content.comment_body: I am working with [product_name] [version_no] ([article_no]) and have enabled cloud access. Here are my questions: For [product_name] Soft Comfort - 1. How do I download a circuit diagram to [product_name]? (Not a network project) 2. Is there a way to update the device time to the cloud if there's only one [product_name] in the network? 3. What does "Diagnostic: Network Error" in network input mean? Is it just for logging? 4. How can I configure an analog input to accept values greater than 65535 using the extended analog input for integer/float conversion? Most special functions only support ranges like -32767 to 32767 or -20000 to +20000. 5. What is a shift register typically used for? 6. What is the difference between a web user and a web guest user? Also, how can I design and use the [product_name] app? I found one on the Google Play Store but don't have a device to install it. For [product_name] Web Editor: 7. Where are passwords stored on AWS? Can I change the password without [product_name] Web Editor? 8. Sometimes I can set the size of an object above 300x300, but other times I can't. I'm using the same object (Trend View) and have increased the screen size to 1500x1500 beforehand. 9. What is the purpose of the Tag Table? Is there a way to change configurations without relinking all objects and tags? 10. How can I prevent [product_name] Web Editor from automatically converting “&” to “&” in the HTTP live stream address? 11. Are there any tutorials for creating custom components for [product_name] Web Editor, or official libraries for user-made components?

1.) The process for downloading a single diagram is the same as for a network project—use symbols or navigate to Tools > Transfer > PC to [product_name]. 2.) I'm not certain about cloud features since I don't use it. 3.) The network input switches HIGH if [product_name] detects a network error while exchanging data with other devices. 4.) Analog signals in [product_name] use integer values, typically in the "signed" format with a range of -32,768 to 32,767. 5.) A shift register is useful for step chains, menu control, and similar sequences. 6.) The web user can operate features like changing setpoints and switching, while the web guest can only view data. 7.) Sorry, I'm not familiar with cloud functions. 8.) I'm unable to assist without seeing your project. 9.) The Tag Table lets you assign global symbolic names for easier management. 10.) Preventing HTML conversion isn't possible with [product_name] Web Editor; perhaps HTML5 could help. 11.) No, there aren't tutorials for custom components.

My goal is to display light sensor readings with ranges up to 65535 or 100000. The resolution is only 1000, and I can't display additional zeros using [product_name] Web Editor. I uploaded both projects—one allows resizing the trend view over 300x300, the other does not—please review the trendview page. Additionally, I can't modify settings in the IoT thing table after removing nearly all objects. It still says IoT things are referenced and cannot be modified or deleted. How can I unlock the IoT Table?
I can't provide information since, as stated earlier, I don't use the cloud and don't intend to.

I checked the trendview page in the project where resizing isn't possible; it's set to 1000x1000. I was able to enlarge the trend view to a maximum of 950x950 on this page. Please see the attached file.
After adjusting the resolution and adding the object again, I am now able to resize it beyond 300x300. Thank you, [user_name].
It appears the limitation is the screen size minus 50. For a screen size of 300x300, the maximum allowed is 250x250.

analysis.insight_summary: Users report various limitations and unclear behaviors when using [product_name] Soft Comfort [version_no] and [product_name] Web Editor [version_no], particularly with cloud-enabled [product_name] hardware. Challenges include analog value display, object sizing, password management, restrictions when modifying IoT thing tables, and understanding functions like shift registers, tag tables, and web user roles. Users also struggle with editing constraints, error messages, and a lack of comprehensive documentation or guidance for component customization.
analysis.user_expectations: Users expect clear instructions for downloading circuit diagrams, flexible options for analog input ranges, simple and unconstrained visualization resizing, straightforward tag and object modification, clarity regarding web user and guest differences, easy app design alternatives, thorough tutorials, and efficient tools for customizing and managing cloud integration and password settings.
